# ProblemList-jdk25u-v1.txt
#
# jdk25u (JDK 25 update) copy of ProblemList-riscv64-qemu-usermode-v11.txt.
# Initial copy for pipeline bring-up; entries are pruned at runtime against the
# jdk25u source tree and this file is maintained during debugging.
#
# Tests excluded from QEMU user-mode CI execution.
# These tests fail due to QEMU environment limitations, NOT JDK code bugs.
# They should be verified on FPGA or real hardware.
#
# Format: <test> <bug_id> <platform>
# Using "QEMU" as pseudo-bug-id for environment-specific exclusions.
###############################################################################

###############################################################################
# Root cause: QEMU user-mode thread scheduling differs from native,
# causing object monitor enter races to behave differently.
###############################################################################


###############################################################################
# Category B: IR Framework socket/thread timeout
# Root cause: IR Framework tests launch a Test VM subprocess via QEMU.
# Under concurrent execution (TEST_JOBS=6), multiple QEMU JVM startups
# compete for CPU, causing jtreg per-test timeout to expire while the
# serverSocket.accept() thread is still waiting for the Test VM to connect.
# The leftover thread triggers "Error while cleaning up threads after test".
###############################################################################

###############################################################################
# Category E: SA (Serviceability Agent) — cross-architecture attach impossible
# Root cause: SA uses ptrace to attach to the target JVM process. Under QEMU
# user-mode, the JVM process is actually a QEMU process (x86), but SA expects
# a RISC-V process. The architecture mismatch causes DebuggerException.
###############################################################################
serviceability/sa/ClhsdbCDSCore.java QEMU generic-all
serviceability/sa/ClhsdbCDSJstackPrintAll.java QEMU generic-all
serviceability/sa/ClhsdbFindPC.java#no-xcomp-core QEMU generic-all
serviceability/sa/ClhsdbFindPC.java#xcomp-core QEMU generic-all
serviceability/sa/ClhsdbPmap.java#core QEMU generic-all
serviceability/sa/ClhsdbPstack.java#core QEMU generic-all
serviceability/sa/CDSJMapClstats.java QEMU generic-all

###############################################################################
# Category F: RSS/memory reporting inaccurate under QEMU
# Root cause: /proc/self/status RSS reports host QEMU process memory, not the
# emulated JVM's actual physical memory usage. AlwaysPreTouch test checks
# RSS >= heap size, which fails because QEMU doesn't map guest pages 1:1.
###############################################################################

gc/TestAlwaysPreTouchBehavior.java#G1 QEMU generic-all

gc/TestAlwaysPreTouchBehavior.java#Z QEMU generic-all

# Additional exclusions from pipeline 1094889 (RVA23 UserMode) analysis
# Added: 2026-08-05
###############################################################################

# Category I: CPU feature detection dead zone (user-mode hwprobe omits V)
# Root cause: QEMU user-mode hwprobe does not advertise the V extension, so
# HotSpot disables ext_Zvkn ("missing dependent extension(s): v (disabled)")
# and vm.cpu.features ends up as "rv64 rva rvc rvd rvf rvi rvm zba zbb zbs
# zfh zfhmin" -- containing neither "aes" nor "zvkn". The upstream guard from
# JDK-8353695, @requires !(vm.cpu.features ~= ".*aes.*" | ~= ".*zvkn.*"),
# therefore fails to exclude the test, while -XX:+UseZvkn on the command line
# still enables AES intrinsics -- so the expected warning "AES instructions are
# not available on this CPU" is never printed and testUseAES fails.
# NOT a JDK code bug. Remove this entry once running in QEMU system-mode (real
# kernel hwprobe reports V + Zvkn) or once user-mode hwprobe advertises V.
# NOTE: the same dead zone silently SKIPS 24 rvv/zvkn-gated tests (including
# compiler/cpuflags/TestAESIntrinsicsOnSupportedConfig.java) -- coverage gap
# tracked separately, do not treat this exclusion as closing that issue.
compiler/cpuflags/TestAESIntrinsicsOnUnsupportedConfig.java QEMU generic-all

###############################################################################
# Additional exclusions from pipeline 1104656 analysis
# Added: 2026-08-12
###############################################################################

# Category: C2 IR Framework socket unsupported in QEMU user-mode (18 tests)
# Root cause: the C2 IR test framework (compiler.lib.ir_framework) starts a
# helper process and connects to the test JVM via a TCP socket. Under QEMU
# user-mode emulation the socket connect/close fails ("Internal Test
# Framework exception - please file a bug: Could not close socket" /
# "Error while cleaning up threads after test"), so every @IR test errors
# out regardless of compiler correctness.
# Introduced visibility in pipeline 1104656 (jtreg 8.3 @requires reevaluation
# now executes these tests instead of skipping them).
# NOT a JDK code bug. Remove these entries once running in QEMU system-mode
# or once user-mode networking supports the IR framework socket protocol.

# Category: CI environment issues (from pipeline 1117256 / 1118193 analysis)
# 1) jdk/jshell/LocalStopExecutionTest.java: test hardcodes 30x1s stop-retry window;
#    under QEMU user-mode, jshell snippet compilation takes >30s, stop() silently
#    returns during compilation (userCodeRunning=false), all 30 retries exhausted.
#    Failing consistently since 08-23 (3 of 4 runs). NOT a JDK code bug - the test
#    is not robust for slow environments. Tracked in SystemMode SM_targeted_langtools.
# 2) java/util/zip/ZipFile/ZipSourceCache.java: Flow pod filesystem reports mtime
#    with second-level granularity; test writes the same zip file twice within
#    the same second -> ZipFile$Source cache key (path+mtime+charset) collides ->
#    stale Source reused (expected 6 but was 5). Environment FS granularity issue.
